incident-bot: ALERT: service=model-serving | SLO breach p95/p99 on embeddings and streaming paths. p99 jumped from 1.2s -> ~4.3s over last 12m. Error rate stable. KV cache slab usage 93%, eviction rate spiked. Prefill vs decode imbalance noted in recent traces. Paging events increased. Paging latency correlates with tail stalls.
Jordan B.: I'm paged, looking. Any customer-facing outage noticed?
Alyssa C.: Metrics: only streaming lanes show degraded throughput/stream stalls; sync generation requests show tail latency increase but less severe. Top affected region: us-west-2.
Marta S.: adding logs: saw lots of small prefill writes filling many slab segments -> fragmentation. Decode threads waiting on page reads.
Lee K.: attaching quick snippet from tail logs: ```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] slab_alloc: seg=0x7f8d index=431 free=12 used=1024
[2026-03-15T14:12:04Z] kv_prefill: key=chat:session:xyz size=48 -> queued write wait=200ms
[2026-03-15T14:12:05Z] decode: waiting_on_page key=chat:session:xyz wait=320ms
```
Sam R.: hypothesis: heavy prefill churn is scattering small entries across slabs, causing fragmentation and more page faults. Prefill writes also evict decode-warm keys leading to prefill vs decode imbalance.
Jordan B.: Can we confirm which model shards are hitting this? Any particular host pools?
Alyssa C.: Heatmap shows dram pressure across pool gpu-pool-5, and hotter on shard set A (shard ids 12-19).
Marta S.: live mitigation candidates: 1) raise slab compaction aggressiveness (cheap) 2) throttle prefill by path (cheap) 3) temporarily redirect streaming to a fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint 4) scale pool by +2 nodes (slower).
Lee K.: I'm for throttling prefill first — it's quick config flip. Patch ready: ```yaml
kv.prefill.rate_limit: 50/s
kv.prefill.batch_size: 4
```
Jordan B.: Who can flip that? Marta, can you apply?
Marta S.: applying now to gpu-pool-5 prefill router... toggling rate limiter. will post when flip done.
ops-bot: Deploy started by Marta S. — change set id cs-87431.
Marta S.: flipped rate limiter. watching metrics.
Alyssa C.: after flip: eviction rate down 40% over 90s, p99 for streaming dropped from 4.3s -> 2.0s. Still above SLO but improving.
Sam R.: ok, next - schedule slab compaction cycle to run immediately with conservative thresholds. Will coordinate with runtime to avoid stall.
Lee K.: initiating compaction on shard set A, running low-priority so decode isn't blocked. Command: `./kvctl compact --shards 12-19 --mode=background`
Jordan B.: good. Any customer impact notes? Which customers saw degraded UX?
Alyssa C.: only customers with streaming long-lived sessions and heavy prefix prefill (like AO chatbots + others). Not all customers. No data exfiltration, no request errors, just latency and some stream stalls.
Marta S.: compaction running, progress 0 -> 12% in 2m. eviction rate trending down. p99 now 1.3s for non-stream; streaming p99 1.9s.
Sam R.: followup: once stable, consider persistent change: increase small-allocation slab buckets and add heuristic to coalesce repeated prefill writes (reduce scatter).
Jordan B.: For now we have mitigations in flight: prefill throttle + background compaction. Scaling not needed. Handoff to next oncall in 30m.
Marta S.: leaving notes in runbook under incident/kv-frag-2026-03-15. Will capture commands and metrics.
Lee K.: adding temporary alert suppression for noisy paging alarms (suppress 10m) to avoid page fatigue while we finish compaction.
ops-bot: Alert suppression enabled by Lee K. for 10m.
Jordan B.: OK handing off to oncall-next. Summary: root cause: kv cache fragmentation from small prefill churn evicting decode-warm entries; actions: throttled prefill, kicked background slab compaction, suppressed noisy alerts. Customer impact: streaming tail latency / stalls for subset of US-W customers; improving. Next steps (post-incident): permanent slab tuning, prefill coalescing, and routing policy changes to avoid pooling hot prefixes on same shards.
Marta S.: tagging @oncall-next to confirm.
Sam R.: if any regression after compaction completes ping me. I can flip scaling if needed.
Jordan B.: logging handoff: handing to oncall-next at 1767555299. Thanks team :thumbsup:
